question: Three agents discuss floating-point rounding. Which position is best supported?
options: Adding zero can change a floating-point value.
Decimal fractions are all represented exactly in binary.
Floating-point arithmetic rounds results to fit finite precision.
gold_answer: Floating-point arithmetic rounds results to fit finite precision.
notes: Team-authored original item on floating-point rounding. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Decimal fractions are all represented exactly in binary.

claims.text: Floating-point addition is not always associative.

evidence.text: Different groupings round intermediate results differently, so the final sums can disagree.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage shows groupings disagreeing, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Double precision eliminates all rounding error.

evidence.text: Doubles only shrink the error; every finite format still rounds most real values.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states doubles still round, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Costs were compared between exact and floating-point implementations.

claims.verdict_rationale: Comparing costs cannot show exact arithmetic is always affordable, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

claims.text: Most decimal fractions have no exact binary representation.

evidence.text: One tenth expands to a repeating binary fraction, so the stored value is only an approximation.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage gives a repeating expansion requiring approximation, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Rounding errors never matter in practice.

evidence.text: Accumulated rounding has visibly corrupted simulations, so numerical care remains essential.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage cites corrupted simulations, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Rounding modes are irrelevant to results.

evidence.text: Outputs were recorded under two rounding settings.

claims.verdict_rationale: Recording outputs cannot show the modes are irrelevant, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Floating-point arithmetic rounds results to fit finite precision.

claims.text: Adding many small numbers to a large one can lose the small ones.

evidence.text: When magnitudes differ greatly, small addends fall off the end of the finite mantissa.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes small addends lost from the mantissa, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Integers beyond two to the fifty-third are all exactly representable in doubles.

evidence.text: Past two to the fifty-third, doubles skip integers, so large counts lose exactness.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states integers are skipped, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Computers do arithmetic without any error.

evidence.text: Error sources were listed for the numerical pipeline.

claims.verdict_rationale: Listing sources cannot show arithmetic is error-free, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
